note: Structural token accounting is exact and hardware independent. Timings and peak memory are this machine only. Two corrections are recorded here because the first revision of this artifact was measured with weights that never loaded: the base checkpoint stores `model.*` keys, so `load_state_dict(strict=False)` into a bare AutoModel matched zero tensors and the backbone ran at its random initialization. It also varied only each state's `id`, so both states tokenized identically and the measurement included whole-question reuse on top of prefix sharing. Weights now load strictly and the states carry different text.

corrections.weights: loaded strictly; base checkpoint remapped from `model.*` and the `lm_head` dropped
corrections.states: distinct text per state, so no whole-question reuse is included
corrections.cpu_regression: On CPU float32 the shared path is slower for small candidate counts (measured 0.73x at K=4) because the per-question prefix prefill and the additive 4D mask cost more than they save when the prefix is short and K is small. MPS measured 1.85x at K=4. Production runs CUDA bf16, which was not available here.
